system.name: SSDO
system.one_liner: a fast solver-free algorithm for traffic engineering in large-scale data center networks

content.subject: how re-splitting one demand's routing across a direct and an indirect path lowers the network's max link utilization

elements.name: Capacity
elements.role: table column giving each link's capacity (all equal to 2)

elements.name: Demand
elements.role: table column giving each node pair's traffic demand: (A,B)=2, (A,C)=1, (B,C)=1

elements.name: B
elements.role: destination of the (A,B) demand and one endpoint of the (B,C) demand

elements.name: C
elements.role: destination of the (A,C) demand and the other endpoint of the (B,C) demand; also the indirect relay for rerouted (A,B) traffic

elements.name: Optimize f_ABC, f_ABB
elements.role: block arrow naming the split-ratio variables being optimized between the initial and optimal panels

relations.what: direct edge, capacity 2, carries the (A,B) demand
direct edge, capacity 2, carries the (A,C) demand
direct edge, capacity 2, carries the (B,C) demand
in the optimal condition, 0.5 units of the (A,B) demand are rerouted through C instead of the direct A-B edge
the rerouted 0.5 units complete their indirect path back to B

panels.label: (c) Initial traffic condition
panels.differs: all three demands take only their direct edge: A-B carries 2/2 (fully saturated), A-C carries 1/2, B-C carries 1/2, giving a maximum link utilization of 1

panels.label: (d) Optimal traffic condition
panels.differs: 0.5 units of the (A,B) demand are rerouted via C: A-B now carries 1.5/2, A-C carries an added 0.5 alongside its own 1/2, and the rerouted flow returns C-to-B at 0.5/2, lowering the maximum link utilization to 0.75

values.what: link capacities (all 2), demand volumes ((A,B)=2, (A,C)=1, (B,C)=1), and the per-edge used/capacity fractions in the initial (2/2, 1/2, 1/2) versus optimal (1.5/2, 1/2, 0.5/2, 1/2, 0.5/2) conditions
values.linked_by: colour: blue for the (A,B) demand and its flow, purple for (A,C), green for (B,C), consistent across the table, topology, and both flow diagrams
values.result_cells: each edge is annotated 'used/capacity' (e.g. '1.5/2'); the maximum fraction across all edges drops from 1 (initial MLU) to 0.75 (optimal MLU)

content.key_idea: Holding the (A,C) and (B,C) split ratios fixed and only re-optimizing the (A,B) demand's routing across the direct edge and an indirect A-C-B path lowers the network's maximum link utilization from 1.0 to 0.75.
content.reading_order: top-left table gives each link's capacity and each pair's demand; top-right shows the shared triangle topology; bottom-left shows the initial all-direct routing (MLU 1); the optimize arrow leads to bottom-right's rebalanced routing (MLU 0.75)

green text/arrows for the (B,C) demand and its flow, consistent across the table, topology, and both flow diagrams
purple text/arrows for the (A,C) demand and its flow
blue text/arrow for the (A,B) demand's direct-edge flow

style.stroke: thin black outlines for the table and node circles; coloured arrow strokes matching each demand
style.arrows: thin coloured arrows with solid heads for each demand's flow, plus one bold horizontal block arrow labelled 'Optimize f_ABC, f_ABB' linking the initial to the optimal panel

encoding.color_means: blue marks the (A,B) demand and its flows, purple marks (A,C), green marks (B,C); the same three colours recur unchanged from the table through the topology into both flow diagrams
encoding.line_style_means: straight arrows are direct-edge flows; the one curved blue arrow in the optimal condition marks the rerouted portion of the (A,B) demand taking the indirect A-C-B path
encoding.state_means: initial vs optimal states are told apart by the fraction labels on each edge (e.g. 2/2 becoming 1.5/2) and by the new curved reroute arrow and its matching C-to-B return arrow
encoding.marker_means: fraction labels ('used/capacity', e.g. '1/2') on every edge double as both the identifying marker and the worked value
encoding.emphasis: the bold block arrow captioned 'Optimize f_ABC, f_ABB' visually separates cause from effect, and the new curved blue arrow in the optimal panel draws the eye straight to what changed
reusable_patterns: a table of capacities/demands feeding a shared topology, then the same topology redrawn before/after an optimization step with per-edge used/capacity fractions and one demand's colour split across a direct and a rerouted arrow

summary: This figure walks through SSDO's subproblem-optimization (SO) mechanic on a 3-node triangle network. The table (a) and topology (b) set up the input: each of the three edges (A-B, A-C, B-C) has capacity 2, and three demands, (A,B)=2 in blue, (A,C)=1 in purple, (B,C)=1 in green, share it. In the initial traffic condition (c), all demands take their direct edge, saturating A-B at 2/2 and giving a maximum link utilization (MLU) of 1. Optimizing only the (A,B) demand's split ratios (labelled f_ABC, f_ABB) while holding the other two demands fixed produces the optimal condition (d): 1.5 of the 2 units still cross A-B directly, but 0.5 are rerouted via C, adding a curved A-to-C arrow and a return C-to-B arrow. The four edges now sit at 0.75, 0.75, 0.5, and 0.25 of capacity, lowering the MLU from 1 to 0.75.
summary_zh: 该图走读SSDO子问题优化：(a)(b)给三角网容量与三需求（蓝A-B=2、紫A-C=1、绿B-C=1）；(c)初始全直连A-B满载2/2，MLU=1；调分流比得(d)最优，四边0.75/0.75/0.5/0.25，MLU降至0.75。
notes: layout.panel_count is set to 4 (matching the figure's four lettered sub-figures a/b/c/d) even though the index's raw panel count is 1; layout.panels/column/aspect mirror the index value as instructed. content.panels lists only (c) and (d), the actual before/after evolution pair, since (a) the capacity/demand table and (b) the topology are setup panels rather than frames of a changing instance.
